purpose: Documentation of the populated pilot authoring contract. Worker module is canonical; this file is not a client assessment endpoint.
outcome: Build a request with “I would like …”.
newStructures: optional bitte after möchte or at end

teachingSteps.title: A quick starting point
teachingSteps.text: Have you learned German before? This helps us avoid crediting the lesson for something you already know. You can choose “I don’t know yet”.
teachingSteps.prompt: If you already can, ask for water in a full German sentence. Otherwise leave this blank.
teachingSteps.companion: We can start from the beginning.

teachingSteps.title: One useful request
teachingSteps.text: ich means I. möchte means would like. Tee means tea. Put them together in that order: Ich möchte Tee. You are making a request, not saying that you already have tea. German writes Tee with a capital letter because it is a noun. We will change just the drink first.
teachingSteps.companion: Let’s work out one small pattern.

teachingSteps.title: Check the meaning
teachingSteps.text: What is the speaker doing with “Ich möchte Tee”?
hints: möchte describes what the person would like.

teachingSteps.title: Change just the drink
teachingSteps.text: Wasser means water. Keep the first two pieces of the request. You will choose the final piece yourself.

teachingSteps.title: Make your own request
teachingSteps.text: The examples are put away. Take the time you need.
teachingSteps.prompt: At a café, ask for water in a full German sentence.
teachingSteps.companion: You have the pieces. Try putting them together.
hints: Start with the person making the request. What comes after “I”?
Use “would like” before the drink in this pattern.
Ich möchte …

teachingSteps.title: One more useful word
teachingSteps.text: Kaffee means coffee. Use the same request pattern with this new drink.

teachingSteps.title: Make your own request
teachingSteps.text: The examples are put away. Take the time you need.
teachingSteps.prompt: At a café, ask for coffee in a full German sentence.
teachingSteps.companion: You have the pieces. Try putting them together.
hints: Start with the person making the request. What comes after “I”?
Use “would like” before the drink in this pattern.
Ich möchte …

teachingSteps.title: Add a polite touch
teachingSteps.text: bitte means please. You can put it at the end of this request. You may also put it after möchte: Ich möchte bitte Tee. Both positions work. The meaning stays the same.

teachingSteps.title: Make your own request
teachingSteps.text: The examples are put away. Take the time you need.
teachingSteps.prompt: At a café, ask for water in a full German sentence, including “please”.
teachingSteps.companion: You have the pieces. Try putting them together.
hints: Start with the person making the request. What comes after “I”?
Use “would like” before the drink in this pattern.
Ich möchte …

teachingSteps.title: Make your own request
teachingSteps.text: The examples are put away. Take the time you need.
teachingSteps.prompt: At a café, ask for coffee in a full German sentence, including “please”.
teachingSteps.companion: You have the pieces. Try putting them together.
hints: Start with the person making the request. What comes after “I”?
Use “would like” before the drink in this pattern.
Ich möchte …

teachingSteps.title: Choose what you want
teachingSteps.text: Imagine you are ordering for yourself. Choose tea, water or coffee and write your request. This is meaningful reuse; it may be a sentence you have already made.
teachingSteps.prompt: What would you like to drink?
hints: Choose your drink first, then use the request pattern.
Ich möchte …

teachingSteps.title: Bring this pattern back later
teachingSteps.text: Your attempts and the help you used are saved separately from lesson completion. A short return tomorrow will help you find out what you can retrieve. You can choose any lesson next.

rules: Keep target subject, object, action and question meaning
When please is required, include bitte
Accept optional gern/gerne and natural drink articles without counting extra combinations
NFC normalize; do not remove umlaut distinction

misconceptions.example: Ich möchte Tee. for a water prompt
misconceptions.cue: Check which drink the listener should understand.
Put möchte after Ich, and the drink after möchte.
The umlaut distinguishes would like from liked.
Check Wasser; do not repeat an unrelated grammar lecture.

assessmentRules.externalHelpDetection: Not possible; research must observe/report outside assistance
